title: Which code opens the lock?
description: A three digit lock has five clues, each telling how many digits of a guess are right and whether they are in place. The clues are used one by one to find the code. Keeko doubts this and thinks two is the first digit.
teaching_notes: One idea: a clue is used by ruling digits in or out, and one deduction feeds the next. Watch for children who trust a digit because it appears often, instead of checking each clue.

source: Find the 3-digit code from the five clues: 265 one right and
video_script.why: The child sees that a clue becomes useful only when it is combined with the others.
video_script.substitution: The five clues of the lock puzzle from the book.
video_script.anchor: A lock with three digit wheels and five clue cards: two six five, two seven one, zero three six, zero six four and five four two
video_script.wrong_move: Trusts a digit because it leads two of the clues, without checking where the other clues allow it.
video_script.payoff_line: The code is four one five.

final_answer.spoken: the code is four one five

maths_rules: clue 036 has nothing right, so 0, 3 and 6 are out
clue 064 has one digit right but misplaced; 0 and 6 are out, so 4 is in the code and not in the last place
clue 542 has two digits right but misplaced; 4 is not in the middle, so 4 is first
clue 265 has one digit right and in place; 6 is out and 2 cannot be first, so 5 is last
clue 542: the two right digits are 5 and 4, so 2 is out
clue 271 has one digit right but misplaced; it is 7 or 1; only the middle place is free and 7 is in the middle in that clue, so 1 goes in the middle
check: the code fits all five clues
video_script.design: One lock with three wheels and five clue cards. Each deduction fills or crosses out a wheel position.
open_questions: The worklist step list is garbled in its sixth step, so this script uses its own deduction, which reaches the same code.

<bookmark mark='m2'/>The second is two seven one, with one digit right but misplaced. The third is zero three six, with nothing right.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The fourth is zero six four, with one digit right but misplaced. The fifth is five four two, with two digits right but misplaced.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, start with the third clue. Nothing is right, so zero, three and six are out.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>In the fourth clue, zero and six are already out.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That leaves four as its right digit. Four is misplaced there, so four is not in the last place.

beats.on_screen: 542: 4 is in the middle, but misplaced, so 4 is first; 265: 6 is out, 2 cannot be first, so 5 is last

marks.m2: 4 is written in the first box
marks.m3: 6 is crossed out in the clue 265 and 2 is shown not fitting the first box
marks.m4: 5 is written in the last box

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, use the fifth clue. Four is misplaced there too, so four is not in the middle.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Four is not in the middle or the last place, so four must be first.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>In the first clue, two six five, six is out. Two cannot be first, because four is first.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The one right digit must be five, in the last place.

beats.on_screen: 542: right digits are 5 and 4, so 2 is out; 271: 7 or 1; 7 is already in the middle there, so 1 goes in the middle; code: 4, 1, 5

marks.m1: 5 and 4 are circled in the clue 542 and 2 is crossed out
marks.m3: 7 is shown already in the middle and 1 slides into the middle box

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, use the fifth clue again. Its two right digits are five and four, so two is out.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The second clue has one right digit, misplaced. Two is out, so it is seven or one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Only the middle place is free. Seven is in the middle in that clue, so it is not misplaced there. One goes in the middle.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the code is 415; check: clue 265 has 5 in place; 271 has 1 misplaced; 036 has nothing; 064 has 4 misplaced; 542 has 5 and 4 misplaced
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The code is four one five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Check the clues. In the first, five is in place, and in the second, one is misplaced.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The third has nothing right. In the fourth, four is misplaced, and in the fifth, five and four are misplaced.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the lock and the clue cards
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt: two is the first digit; the clues put four first and rule two out, and the doubt is struck through

marks.m1: the doubt appears as a bubble over the first wheel

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks two is the first digit, because two leads the first and second clues.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But a digit that leads a clue need not be in the code. Four is first, and two is not in the code at all.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Check every clue before trusting a guess.
